key_insight: Linking displacement-sampling distance to mesh resolution enables convergent stress intensity factor estimates where conventional nearest-tip sampling fails.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stress intensity factors support accurate decisions about whether pre-existing fractures will propagate in numerical simulations.
method: Balance near-tip asymptotic truncation error against numerical discretization error.
Use the resulting scaling law to select sampling distances for two-point displacement correlation.
Test standard quadratic finite elements, quarter-point quadratic finite elements, and multi-point stress approximation finite volumes.
evidence_signal: Across fracture benchmarks with pure-mode and mixed-mode loading, all three discretization methods showed decreasing SIF errors with scaling-based sampling as meshes were refined, unlike nearest-tip sampling.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the scaling formula or its applicability beyond the tested methods and benchmarks.
paper_title: A scaling law for numerical computation of fracture stress intensity factors
